data.claim: inherited_deps adds every ancestor's needs unless the task is tagged decide; research/doc tasks with doc-only globs get no exemption
data.falsifier: a research task with doc globs under a needing phase is ready in ddflow next
data.mechanism: core/schedule.py inherited_deps returns early only for is_decide
data.probe_output: FAILED: N-res, N-docs absent from ready; passes after the exemption
data.question: Why is a research/doc task under a phase that needs another phase blocked?

evidence.note: research note CONFIRMED; test failed before fix
read ddflow brief --item; no governing decision conflicts
commit docs-only tasks do not inherit phase needs

chunk_findings.detail: `_docs_only_exempt` calls `path_in_glob(g, d)` where `g` is an element of `it.globs` (a glob pattern) and `d` is an element of `cfg.gates.doc_globs` (also a glob pattern). `path_in_glob` is the imported alias for `inside`, a predicate that checks whether a concrete path is inside a glob pattern, so this is checking whether the literal glob string `"docs/**"` matches the doc-glob string `"docs/*"`, not whether every file matched by the task glob is a document. For example, with `[gates].doc_globs = ["docs/*"]` and a task with `globs = ["docs/**"]` (which also matches code files under subdirectories), the literal string `"docs/**"` is matched by `"docs/*"` because `*` absorbs the literal `**` component, causing `_docs_only_exempt` to return True and a non-doc-only task to skip inherited phase dependencies. The check must reason about glob language/subset or use a glob-overlap predicate, not `path_in_glob`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule.py:_docs_only_exempt

chunk_findings.detail: The new logic does not implement the documented `docs_ignore_phase_needs` contract. For `[gates].doc_globs = ["docs/**"]` and a docs-only task with `globs = ["docs/**/*.md"]`, the line `if "**" in glob: return False` makes `_glob_is_docs` return `False` because the task glob contains `**` and is not literally in `doc_globs`. Every path matching `docs/**/*.md` is under `docs/**` and therefore a document per the config, but the task still inherits the phase's `needs` and remains blocked.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule.py:_glob_is_docs

chunk_findings.detail: The `*`/`?` probe is not a sound inclusion test. With `[gates].doc_globs = ["docs/x*"]` and a task glob `docs/*`, the probe is `docs/x`; `path_in_glob("docs/x", "docs/x*")` is true, so `_docs_only_exempt` skips phase dependencies. But `docs/*` also matches `docs/y`, which is not in `doc_globs`; hence a task that can write non-doc files is incorrectly exempted from `phase.needs`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule.py:_glob_is_docs

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 1 still holds. With `[gates].doc_globs = ["docs/**"]` and a docs-only task whose `globs = ["docs/**/*.md"]`, `_glob_is_docs` returns `False` because `"**" in glob` and the task glob is not literally in `doc_globs`. Every path matched by `docs/**/*.md` is under `docs/**`, so all task globs are documents under the documented contract, yet the task still inherits the phase `needs` and can remain blocked. The current probe logic does not address this branch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule.py:_glob_is_docs

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 2 still holds in substance despite the added second probe. With `[gates].doc_globs = ["docs/x", "docs/zq9"]` and a task glob `docs/*`, `_glob_is_docs` produces the probes `docs/x` and `docs/zq9`; both are doc globs, so it returns `True`. But `docs/*` also matches `docs/y`, which is not in `doc_globs`, so a task that can match/write non-doc files is incorrectly exempted from `phase.needs`. Finite probe strings are not a sound inclusion test for glob languages.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule.py:_glob_is_docs

chunk_findings.detail: The previous probe still holds. With `[gates].doc_globs = ["docs/**"]` and a docs-only task whose `globs = ["docs/**/*.md"]`, `_glob_is_docs` returns `False` because the task glob contains `**` and is not literally present in `doc_globs`. Every path matching `docs/**/*.md` is under the configured doc glob, so the task is docs-only and should be exempt from `phase.needs`, but it still inherits them and remains blocked. The reviewed part does not alter this branch, so the defect is still present.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule.py:_glob_is_docs

chunk_findings.detail: The previous `*`/`?` probe is still not a sound inclusion test. With `[gates].doc_globs = ["docs/x*"]` and a task glob `docs/*`, the probe checks `docs/x`; `path_in_glob("docs/x", "docs/x*")` is true, so `_docs_only_exempt` skips phase dependencies. But `docs/*` also matches `docs/y`, which is not in `doc_globs`; a task that can write non-doc files is therefore incorrectly exempted from `phase.needs`. The reviewed part leaves this probe unchanged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule.py:_glob_is_docs

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier finding still holds. The new tests do not cover the failing input `[gates].doc_globs = ["docs/**"]` with a docs-only task whose `globs = ["docs/**/*.md"]`. `test_docs_only_tasks_are_ready_code_tasks_still_wait` uses only `docs/n.md` and `docs/ddflow/research/n.md`, and `test_a_recursive_glob_is_not_docs_under_a_narrower_doc_glob` exercises the opposite containment (`docs/**` task glob under narrower `docs/*`). With the branch `if "**" in glob: return False`, `_glob_is_docs("docs/**/*.md", ["docs/**"])` still returns `False`, so such a docs-only task still inherits `phase.needs` and remains blocked even though every path it matches is under `docs/**`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule.py:_glob_is_docs

chunk_findings.detail: Defaulting this knob to `True` makes the still-unsound `_glob_is_docs` predicate active for every schedule without any user opt-in. For example, with `[gates].doc_globs = ["docs/x*"]` and a task whose `globs = ["docs/*"]`, `_glob_is_docs` returns `True` because it probes only `docs/x`, but `docs/*` also matches `docs/y`, which is not a document glob. With this new default, that task is exempted from `phase.needs` and can be offered before the phase dependencies it must wait on. The previous review already identified this false positive in `_glob_is_docs`; setting the switch to `True` by default turns that classification bug into the default scheduling behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/schedule.py:192 docs_ignore_phase_needs

chunk_findings.detail: With `[gates].doc_globs = ["docs/**/*.md"]` and a research task `globs = ["docs/**/research.md"]`, every path the task glob can match (for example `docs/foo/research.md`) is also matched by the doc glob, so the task is docs-only and should be exempt from inherited phase `needs`. But `_glob_is_docs("docs/**/research.md", ["docs/**/*.md"])` returns `False`: the doc glob is not an exact match, does not end in `/**`, is not `dir/*`, and does not start with `**/`; the fallback `return not any(c in glob for c in "*?[") and any(...)` is skipped because the task glob contains `*`. As a result `_docs_only_exempt` returns `False`, `inherited_deps` still adds the phase's ancestor deps, and the docs-only task remains blocked, so the bug is not fixed for this valid doc-glob configuration.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule.py:_glob_is_docs
